evidence.claim: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.title: Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional text; directly states presidential powers and military command relation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Bolsonaro held this office throughout 2022; the source is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Legal authority does not show how Bolsonaro used it in nuclear or existential-risk matters.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro repeated false claims about the electronic voting system to foreign diplomats and attacked TSE ministers without evidence, months before the election.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro chama embaixadores para atacar processo eleitoral; TSE rebate
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro repeated false claims about the electronic voting system to foreign diplomats and attacked TSE ministers without evidence, months before the election.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs describing the diplomatic event and its contents
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with direct description of the president's own remarks.
contrary_evidence: This is incitement and misinformation rather than physical violence, but it materially raised the domestic fear climate.

evidence.claim: The TSE found that Bolsonaro's motociata and temple event in Cuiabá constituted premature campaign propaganda.
evidence.title: TSE multa Jair Bolsonaro, candidato à reeleição à Presidência, por propaganda antecipada
evidence.excerpt: The TSE found that Bolsonaro's motociata and temple event in Cuiabá constituted premature campaign propaganda.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph summarizing the court ruling
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary electoral-court ruling on Bolsonaro's own campaign conduct.
contrary_evidence: A single sanction does not by itself prove a full pattern of capture, but it is directly relevant to manipulation of the campaign environment.

evidence.claim: The TSE barred the use of images from Bolsonaro's official trips in campaign material to preserve equal opportunity in the race.
evidence.title: Imagens de Bolsonaro em viagem como chefe de Estado não podem ser usadas em campanha
evidence.excerpt: The TSE barred the use of images from Bolsonaro's official trips in campaign material to preserve equal opportunity in the race.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary court order directly addressing misuse of official state imagery in the campaign.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro as incumbent candidate and head of state.
contrary_evidence: The order is a constraint on misuse, not evidence that Bolsonaro voluntarily self-bound.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said Bolsonaro claimed the voting system was susceptible to fraud, challenged the election results in court in late November, and that the TSE rejected the case as bad faith; it also described the 2022 campaign as marked by disinformation, harassment, and political violence.
evidence.title: Brazil: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said Bolsonaro claimed the voting system was susceptible to fraud, challenged the election results in court in late November, and that the TSE rejected the case as bad faith; it also described the 2022 campaign as marked by disinformation, harassment, and political violence.
evidence.source_locator: Key Developments in 2022 and the Electoral Process / D1 sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major comparative democracy report synthesizing target-year events and institutional responses.
evidence.period_fit: Summarizes the target year 2022 with direct relevance to Bolsonaro's campaign conduct.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro conduct on fraud claims; institutional response by the TSE; broader violence environment also involved other actors.
contrary_evidence: The same report says Brazil remained a democracy with competitive elections, so this is erosive conduct rather than outright authoritarian closure.

evidence.claim: The government dismissed the IPEA president and named Erik Figueiredo, then the Economy Ministry's subsecretary of fiscal policy, as his replacement to make the institute more propositive.
evidence.title: Governo exonera presidente do Ipea e nomeia auxiliar de Guedes como substituto
evidence.excerpt: The government dismissed the IPEA president and named Erik Figueiredo, then the Economy Ministry's subsecretary of fiscal policy, as his replacement to make the institute more propositive.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and the description of Figueiredo's prior role
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting through a major Brazilian outlet on a concrete appointment inside the economic policy apparatus.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro-administration appointment, but the evidence is about staffing rather than economic outcomes.
contrary_evidence: A technocratic appointment is only weak evidence of competence unless paired with results.

evidence.claim: The government planned to veto R$3.1 billion in budget items to fund payroll, while leaving the electoral fund at R$4.9 billion, a politically difficult choice in an election year.
evidence.title: Brazil government to veto 3.1 billion reais in budget items to fund payroll -sources
evidence.excerpt: The government planned to veto R$3.1 billion in budget items to fund payroll, while leaving the electoral fund at R$4.9 billion, a politically difficult choice in an election year.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and the section on the electoral fund and payroll allocations
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting based on Ministry of Economy sources and the official budget process.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Bolsonaro administration budget choice, but shaped by Congress and election-year politics.
contrary_evidence: The decision was partly constrained by Congress already having approved the budget bill.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said Bolsonaro and his allies were a key source of election disinformation, that Bolsonaro made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that these claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as a well-financed disinformation machine.
evidence.title: Brazil: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said Bolsonaro and his allies were a key source of election disinformation, that Bolsonaro made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that these claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as a well-financed disinformation machine.
evidence.source_locator: country report narrative under election disinformation discussion
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable independent rights monitor synthesizing contemporaneous evidence and fact-checking counts; not a court finding, but strong secondary documentation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Bolsonaro and his allies; the report ties the statements to his office, campaign, and official communication channels.
contrary_evidence: The report is secondary synthesis, not a judicial finding.
It captures a pattern, not each individual false claim.

evidence.claim: Aos Fatos counted at least 6,042 false or distorted claims by Bolsonaro since the start of his presidency and noted that his repeated falsehoods included claims that his government had no corruption scandals.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro supera 6.000 declarações falsas ou distorcidas no início da campanha pela reeleição
evidence.excerpt: Aos Fatos counted at least 6,042 false or distorted claims by Bolsonaro since the start of his presidency and noted that his repeated falsehoods included claims that his government had no corruption scandals.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and first analytic paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized fact-checking outlet with transparent counting method and direct examples; not an official record but highly relevant on truthfulness.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Bolsonaro-specific; the claims are his own public statements while in office and as a candidate.
contrary_evidence: Fact-check counts do not measure intent for every statement.
The article is a fact-check summary, not a court judgment.

evidence.claim: Aos Fatos concluded Bolsonaro ended his presidency with 6,676 false or distorted statements, including repeated false claims about corruption, the pandemic, the economy, and the Pix payment system.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro mentiu mais de quatro vezes por dia durante governo
evidence.excerpt: Aos Fatos concluded Bolsonaro ended his presidency with 6,676 false or distorted statements, including repeated false claims about corruption, the pandemic, the economy, and the Pix payment system.
evidence.source_locator: sections 'Negacionismo prevalece', 'Mentiras repetidas', and 'Longe do real'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Longitudinal fact-check compilation with explicit counts and recurring themes; strong for pattern evidence, weaker for legal culpability.
evidence.period_fit: Covers 2022 and the end of Bolsonaro's term.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Bolsonaro-specific and attributable to his public record as president and candidate.
contrary_evidence: A fact-check ledger cannot prove motive in every instance.
It is a cumulative press compilation rather than an adjudicated finding.

evidence.claim: The TSE president said the coalition backing Bolsonaro's runoff challenge relied on 'absolutely false' arguments and fined the coalition R$22.9 million for bad-faith litigation over a supposed second-round urn verification.
evidence.title: Moraes condena coligação Pelo Bem do Brasil por litigância de má-fé e aplica multa de R$ 22,9 milhões
evidence.excerpt: The TSE president said the coalition backing Bolsonaro's runoff challenge relied on 'absolutely false' arguments and fined the coalition R$22.9 million for bad-faith litigation over a supposed second-round urn verification.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official electoral-court order with explicit legal finding and sanction.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year, after the runoff.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's coalition and campaign litigation, though the formal party actor was the coalition rather than Bolsonaro alone.
contrary_evidence: The decision targets coalition litigation, not a personal criminal finding against Bolsonaro.
It concerns post-election conduct rather than routine governing.

evidence.claim: The TSE unanimously rejected objections and kept in electoral court the investigation into Bolsonaro and Braga Netto over the July 2022 ambassadors meeting that attacked the voting system with false claims.
evidence.title: TSE mantém na Justiça Eleitoral julgamento de ação de investigação contra Jair Bolsonaro e Braga Netto
evidence.excerpt: The TSE unanimously rejected objections and kept in electoral court the investigation into Bolsonaro and Braga Netto over the July 2022 ambassadors meeting that attacked the voting system with false claims.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official court decision directly addressing Bolsonaro's conduct and the legal basis for scrutiny.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and about a 2022 act.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Bolsonaro-specific: the meeting was hosted by him as president and candidate, with Braga Netto as his ticket mate.
contrary_evidence: This is an investigation-maintenance ruling, not a final merits judgment.
It shows ongoing scrutiny rather than final liability.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro publicly said replacing Petrobras' chief executive was possible after fuel-price criticism and indicated that anyone in government could be replaced if not doing the job satisfactorily.
evidence.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro hints at potential replacement of Petrobras CEO
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro publicly said replacing Petrobras' chief executive was possible after fuel-price criticism and indicated that anyone in government could be replaced if not doing the job satisfactorily.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on Bolsonaro's own statements and their policy context; strong contemporaneous evidence of politicized pressure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's own public pressure on a state company, though the corporate board ultimately remained a separate institutional actor.
contrary_evidence: The statement alone does not prove unlawful self-dealing.
Some intervention was framed as fuel-price policy rather than personal gain.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro's government ousted Petrobras's chief executive for the second time in two months and signaled plans to alter the company's market-based fuel pricing policy after Bolsonaro railed against price increases.
evidence.title: Petrobras shares drop following CEO ouster, fuel price woes
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro's government ousted Petrobras's chief executive for the second time in two months and signaled plans to alter the company's market-based fuel pricing policy after Bolsonaro railed against price increases.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters coverage of a concrete personnel action and policy pressure on a state-controlled company.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro as president, because the article describes his political pressure and the ensuing executive ouster.
contrary_evidence: The move is easier to read as politicized pressure than personal enrichment.
It concerns corporate control rather than private gain.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he had the right to propose changes to Petrobras's board and management and indicated the changes would come soon, framing the company as something he could reshape through the government.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro indica que vai trocar diretoria da Petrobras
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he had the right to propose changes to Petrobras's board and management and indicated the changes would come soon, framing the company as something he could reshape through the government.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs and Bolsonaro quote section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters syndicated report of Bolsonaro's explicit statement about replacing state-company leadership.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Bolsonaro-specific, because it quotes his own public claim of authority over Petrobras management.
contrary_evidence: Corporate governance is partly institutional, so the statement is not itself proof of illegality.
The quote reflects intent and pressure, not the final outcome.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro's government planned to veto R$3.1 billion in discretionary spending, while keeping the electoral fund at R$4.9 billion, because a larger cut would be politically difficult in an election year.
evidence.title: Brazil government to veto 3.1 billion reais in budget items to fund payroll -sources
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro's government planned to veto R$3.1 billion in discretionary spending, while keeping the electoral fund at R$4.9 billion, because a larger cut would be politically difficult in an election year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on an election-year budget choice with clear political tradeoffs.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Bolsonaro's government and election-year incentives, though the budget process also involved Congress and ministries.
contrary_evidence: This is a political-budget tradeoff, not direct personal enrichment.
The article relies on unnamed sources rather than a signed government statement.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro presented a 48-page plan to the TSE with freedom as its central axis and priorities including job and income generation, fiscal consolidation, debt stability, privatization, maintenance of Auxílio Brasil at R$600, education, and technology.
evidence.title: Propostas de Bolsonaro: veja principais pontos do plano de governo
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro presented a 48-page plan to the TSE with freedom as its central axis and priorities including job and income generation, fiscal consolidation, debt stability, privatization, maintenance of Auxílio Brasil at R$600, education, and technology.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and numbered list of proposals
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct summary of the submitted campaign program with concrete priorities; not a measure of execution by itself.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Bolsonaro-specific because it summarizes the program his campaign filed for reelection.
contrary_evidence: A campaign platform shows stated goals, not implementation.
The article itself notes the plan is a set of directives rather than binding commitments.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro's government rolled out a R$273 billion election-year package, including early social-program payments and consignado loans, and that experts saw it as use of the state machine to boost reelection.
evidence.title: Com pacote de R$273 bi, uso da máquina impulsiona Bolsonaro na eleição e não tem punição à vista
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro's government rolled out a R$273 billion election-year package, including early social-program payments and consignado loans, and that experts saw it as use of the state machine to boost reelection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with concrete fiscal figures and a clear implementation claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's government, though some components depended on Congress and broader fiscal conditions.
contrary_evidence: Some measures were shaped by Congress and preexisting fiscal rules.
Election-year spending does not prove durable policy success.
